subject: EdgeNova: performance qualification & A/B test plan vs HyperCloud
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Ben Harper <ben.harper@edgenova.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-11T15:20:00Z
Subject: EdgeNova: performance qualification & A/B test plan vs HyperCloud

Hi Ben —

Great to chat earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we have a single source of truth before the benchmark run:

What we agreed:
- Redwood will run an A/B experiment comparing HyperCloud endpoints (their managed inference) vs Redwood hosted inference for your customer-facing embedding+chat path.
- Primary metrics: p95 and p99 latency (in ms), tokens/sec (aggregate throughput), and tail error rate. We will also report cost per 1M tokens for the test window.
- Target success criteria you flagged: p95 < 200ms for 1–2k token responses and tokens/sec > 4k for sustained concurrent traffic (you said your read-heavy traffic tends to spike to ~80 concurrent users).

Data / artifacts we need from EdgeNova:
1) Representative request payloads (3–5 examples) including sequence lengths and typical system messages
2) A test service account or temporary HyperCloud API key + endpoint for us to call in the A/B harness, or we can provide a small runner you can execute in your environment if preferred
3) Preferred test window (timezone: PST). You mentioned late-evening traffic patterns, so a 3–4 hour window overnight would mirror production load.

Redwood plan and owners:
- Marcus Lin (cc) will own the run and infra config (batching, concurrency, quant profile).
- Jordan Blake will surface readouts and help interpret p95/p99 differences and KV cache behavior.
- I will coordinate logistics, collect artifacts, and share the results + a short decision memo.

What Redwood will measure specifically:
- p50/p95/p99 measured at the client side (request->final token), with breakdowns for generation vs network time.
- Tokens/sec measured as tokens produced per second aggregated over the window and per-second time series for microbursts.
- Cache hit rates for prefix/KV caching (if you use consistent prompts) and per-call cost estimates.
- We will also run a small stress pass to validate tail behavior (burst concurrency up to 120).

Attached: redwood-teaser.pdf (short summary of how our runtime optimizes tail latency and continuous batching).

Next steps (please reply inline):
- Ben: confirm you can provide the sample payloads + HyperCloud API key, and confirm a 3-hour window next week (Jan 17–19) that works.
- Marcus/Jordan: will prepare the harness and the initial config (we plan to test 3 configurations: baseline (no quant), 8-bit quant, and aggressive batching).

Thanks — excited to get this data — Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
From: Ben Harper <ben.harper@edgenova.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeNova Platform Ops <ops@edgenova.com>
Date: 2028-01-12T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: EdgeNova: performance qualification & A/B test plan vs HyperCloud

Thanks Hannah — good summary. We can provide the sample payloads (attached) and will provision a HyperCloud API key for the test. A couple quick clarifications:
- Test duration: 3 hours works for us. Prefer Jan 18 02:00–05:00 PST to match our overnight spike.
- Token budget: expect ~1.2M tokens total across the window based on current traffic estimates. Is that in scope for your run?
- Dedicated capacity: curious whether Redwood can run the Redwood side on a dedicated pool (we'd like to understand difference vs your multi-tenant host).

I attached three typical request examples (short, medium, long). Ops will follow up with the HyperCloud key by end-of-day tomorrow.

Ben
CTO, EdgeNova
ben.harper@edgenova.com

Attachments: edge_samples.json
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ben Harper <ben.harper@edgenova.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-12T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: EdgeNova: performance qualification & A/B test plan vs HyperCloud

On Wed, Jan 12, 2028 at 09:05, Ben Harper <ben.harper@edgenova.com> wrote:
> Thanks Hannah — good summary. We can provide the sample payloads (attached) and will provision a HyperCloud API key for the test.

Thanks Ben — we'll plan for Jan 18 02:00–05:00 PST. Quick technical notes so Marcus can provision the harness: 
- Please confirm peak concurrency target for the run (you mentioned 80 sustained, we'll plan 80 steady + two 30-min bursts to 120)
- Provide a small distribution of sequence lengths (we'll run stepped buckets: 64, 256, 1024 tokens)
- For fairness we'll run the same prompt routing/temperature on both HyperCloud and Redwood and capture end-to-end times from the same client harness.

Marcus: can you draft the runner config (concurrency profile + per-bucket RPS) and share by EOD? We'll also include a run that enables our KV prefix caching to quantify its impact on p95/p99.

-jb
From: Ben Harper <ben.harper@edgenova.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeNova Platform Ops <ops@edgenova.com>
Date: 2028-01-13T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: EdgeNova: performance qualification & A/B test plan vs HyperCloud

Jordan — we will provision the HyperCloud key and ops@edgenova.com is looped in to hand off the service account. Confirming concurrency: 80 steady with two 30-min microbursts to 120 works.

A note on targets: our internal SRE thinks p95 < 200ms is attainable; p99 is the bigger unknown. We're interested in seeing the p99 breakouts by generation length and whether caching or batching drives the majority of wins.

Also yes — if Redwood can present results for both hosted and dedicated runs that would be very helpful. Happy to discuss cost implications after the benchmark.

Ben
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Harper <ben.harper@edgenova.com>
Date: 2028-01-18T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: EdgeNova: performance qualification & A/B test plan vs HyperCloud

Marcus/Jordan — final internal checklist before tonight's run (02:00 PST start):
- Marcus: confirm harness deployed, runner config includes buckets [64,256,1024], concurrency profile (80 steady, two 30-min bursts to 120), and the 3 configs (baseline, 8-bit quant, aggressive batching).
- Jordan: ensure client-side timing instrumentation captures generation vs network split and that we log per-second tokens/sec and per-request latency histogram. Also capture prefix cache hit rate and include a column for 'cache-primed' vs 'cold' requests.
- We will request dedicated capacity for the Redwood side after the hosted run if EdgeNova asks for a dedicated follow-up; include a short cost tab so Ben has an apples-to-apples comparison.

I'll kick off the run and own the writeup. Attaching a placeholder that we will populate with the initial CSV: edge-bench-results.csv

Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
